# Gold-Standard Test Set

> **M-1 fix (REVIEW-2026-07-25): The original README claimed these were
> "expert-annotated real charts" but every entry in `_index.json`
> has `"synthetic": true`. This rewrite accurately reflects that the
> 8 cases are SYNTHETIC images generated by matplotlib, used to
> unit-test the metric math in `rca_core.eval_metrics` and
> `rca_core.quality` — NOT to measure real-world extraction accuracy.**

## What's actually here

Each entry has:

- `image.png` — a **synthetic** chart rendered by matplotlib
  (`tests/fixtures/synthetic_data.py`). Clean horizontal text, no
  handwriting, no rotated/scan artifacts, no overlapping ranges —
  i.e. **not representative of real published range charts**.
- `ground_truth.json` — the label structure that the metric maths
  are asserted against. Synthetic ground truth, not extracted from a
  published chart.
- `synthetic_data.py` — also exposes `make_range_chart(...)` and
  similar helpers used directly by `tests/test_gold_metrics.py`.

## Current Coverage

| Type | Real | Synthetic | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| range_chart | 0 | 3 | 3 |
| columnar_section | 0 | 2 | 2 |
| abundance | 0 | 2 | 2 |
| phylogenetic_tree | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| **Total** | **0** | **8** | **8** |

## What these tests DO validate

- The precision / recall / range-accuracy / biozone / abundance /
  Robinson-Foulds metric implementations in `rca_core/eval_metrics.py`
  produce the expected numbers for well-controlled inputs.
- The quality scorer in `rca_core/quality.py` runs without crashing
  on structured input.
- `_classify_array_item`, `_normalize_*`, `_carry_extras`, etc.
  behave on the synthetic payload shapes.
- **REVIEW-2026-07-31 (gold pipeline gate)**: `model_response.json`
  (deterministic seeded degradation of `ground_truth.json`, generated by
  `_gen_canned.py`) is run through the REAL offline pipeline —
  `safe_json_loads` → `normalize_*` → `eval_metrics` — with precision /
  recall / abundance / topology gates in `tests/test_gold_smoke.py`.
  Regenerate after editing any fixture: `python _gen_canned.py`.

## What these tests DO NOT validate

Because the inputs are clean, noise-free synthetic renders:

- **Real extraction accuracy** — accuracy numbers from these tests do
  **not** generalise to real range charts that have rotated text,
  handwritten overlays, dark-mode journals, scanned PDFs, overlapping
  ranges, ambiguous species names, etc. A VLM that scores 0.95 here
  may score 0.55 on real published charts.
- **Calibration of confidence / quality grades** — the quality scorer
  was tuned against hand-crafted synthetic ground truth, so the A/B/C
  grade boundaries have not been empirically validated against expert
  judgment on real charts.
- **Robustness of the VLM prompt** — the synthetic charts are too
  clean to expose prompt-instruction gaps (e.g. handling Chinese
  stratigraphic terms, open nomenclature sp./cf./aff., biozone
  iron-rule enforcement under handwriting).

## CI Usage

- `pytest -m gold_smoke` — 5 quick cases, every PR (these are
  fixture-only — they do not call the LLM).
- `pytest -m gold` — all 8 cases, weekly cron + release tag (also
  fixture-only).
- `RCA_OFFLINE_GOLD=1` — use cached responses, zero API cost.

The "real" VLM-vs-fixture integration test that the docs reference
(`test_gold_smoke.py`) is `@pytest.mark.skip(reason="Requires live
LLM API")`. Until un-skipped, it does **not** run in CI.

## What is missing

We need **real, expert-annotated** range charts from published
literature (CC-BY/CC0 or with permission) before claiming validated
accuracy numbers. The annotation workflow described in
`ANNOTATION_GUIDE.md` (double-blind, Krippendorff's α ≥ 0.80, ICZN
qualifier table) is the right process — but **no real cases have
been collected yet**. Until they are, treat any accuracy number
quoted in docs / comments / dashboard from this dataset as a
**unit-test result for the metric code**, not as evidence about the
real-world performance of the VLM extractor.

## Adding new cases

To add **synthetic** cases (current mode):

1. Add a new case folder under the relevant type directory.
2. Generate with `scripts/generate_gold_synthetic.py` or
   `tests/fixtures/synthetic_data.py`.
3. Update `_index.json` with `"synthetic": true`.

To add **real** expert-annotated cases (the actually-needed path):

1. Follow `ANNOTATION_GUIDE.md` end-to-end: source capture, license
   verification, double-blind annotation, Krippendorff's α ≥ 0.80.
2. Store the image and ground truth under `tests/fixtures/gold/<type>/<id>/`.
3. Update `_index.json` with `"synthetic": false` and the citation.
4. Un-skip `test_gold_smoke.py` (or write a new integration test) and
   wire it into CI so accuracy numbers track real-world performance.
